QT (Quality Threshold) clustering is an algorithm that builds clusters\n// by starting with a seed point and iteratively adding the closest point\n// that maintains the cluster's diameter below a threshold.\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <limits>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nstatic const double MAX_WIDTH = 20.0;\nstatic const double MAX_HEIGHT = 20.0;\n\n// Structure to represent a point in 2D space\nstruct Point {\n    double x, y;\n};\n\n// Structure to represent a cluster\nstruct Cluster {\n    std::vector<int> members;\n    int seed_point;\n};\n\n// Generate synthetic 2D point data in clusters\nvoid generateSyntheticData(std::vector<Point>& points, const int N, unsigned int seed = 42) {\n    auto frand = [&seed]() mutable { return rand_r(&seed) / static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX); };\n    \n    const double min_dim = std::min(MAX_WIDTH, MAX_HEIGHT);\n    int count = 0;\n    \n    while (count < N) {\n        // Create group_cnt points within a circle of radius R\n        // around center point (cntr_x, cntr_y)\n        const double cntr_x = frand() * MAX_WIDTH;\n        const double cntr_y = frand() * MAX_HEIGHT;\n        const double R = frand() * min_dim / 2.0;\n        int group_cnt = static_cast<int>(frand() * (N / 30.0));\n        \n        // Make sure we don't make more points than we need\n        if (group_cnt > (N - count)) {\n            group_cnt = N - count;\n        }\n        \n        while (group_cnt > 0) {\n            const double sign = (frand() < 0.5) ? -1.0 : 1.0;\n            const double r = frand() * R;\n            const double dx = (2.0 * frand() - 1.0) * r;\n            const double dy = std::sqrt(r * r - dx * dx) * sign;\n            const double x = cntr_x + dx;\n            const double y = cntr_y + dy;\n            \n            if (x < 0 || x > MAX_WIDTH || y < 0 || y > MAX_HEIGHT) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            \n            points[count] = {x, y};\n            count++;\n            group_cnt--;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Calculate Euclidean distance between two points\ninline double distance(const Point& p1, const Point& p2) {\n    double dx = p1.x - p2.x;\n    double dy = p1.y - p2.y;\n    return std::sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);\n}\n\n// Find the closest unclustered point to the current cluster that maintains diameter < threshold\n// Returns -1 if no such point exists\nint findClosestPoint(const std::vector<int>& cluster_members,\n                     const std::vector<bool>& clustered,\n                     const std::vector<bool>& in_cluster,\n                     const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                     const double threshold,\n                     const int point_count) {\n    int closest_point = -1;\n    double min_diameter = std::numeric_limits<double>::max();\n    \n    // Try each unclustered point as a candidate\n    for (int candidate = 0; candidate < point_count; ++candidate) {\n        // Skip if already clustered or already in this cluster\n        if (clustered[candidate] || in_cluster[candidate]) continue;\n        \n        // Calculate the maximum distance from candidate to all cluster members\n        double max_dist = 0.0;\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < cluster_members.size(); ++i) {\n            const int member = cluster_members[i];\n            const double dist = distance(points[candidate], points[member]);\n            max_dist = std::max(max_dist, dist);\n        }\n        \n        // If adding this point keeps diameter below threshold and is better than current best\n        if (max_dist < threshold && max_dist < min_diameter) {\n            min_diameter = max_dist;\n            closest_point = candidate;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return closest_point;\n}\n\n// Generate a candidate cluster starting from a seed point\n// Returns the cardinality (size) of the cluster\nint generateCandidateCluster(const int seed_point,\n                              const std::vector<bool>& clustered,\n                              const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                              const double threshold,\n                              const int point_count,\n                              std::vector<int>* cluster_members = nullptr) {\n    std::vector<bool> in_cluster(point_count, false);\n    std::vector<int> members;\n    \n    // Add seed point\n    in_cluster[seed_point] = true;\n    members.push_back(seed_point);\n    \n    // Iteratively add closest points\n    while (static_cast<int>(members.size()) < point_count) {\n        // Find closest point to current cluster that maintains diameter < threshold\n        const int closest = findClosestPoint(members, clustered, in_cluster, points, \n                                             threshold, point_count);\n        \n        if (closest < 0) break; // No more points can be added\n        \n        in_cluster[closest] = true;\n        members.push_back(closest);\n    }\n    \n    // Copy members if requested\n    if (cluster_members) {\n        *cluster_members = members;\n    }\n    \n    return static_cast<int>(members.size());\n}\n\n// Main QT clustering algorithm\nstd::vector<Cluster> qtClustering(const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                                  const double threshold) {\n    const int N = static_cast<int>(points.size());\n    std::vector<bool> clustered(N, false);\n    std::vector<int> unclustered_indices;\n    std::vector<Cluster> clusters;\n    \n    // Initialize unclustered indices\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) {\n        unclustered_indices.push_back(i);\n    }\n    \n    // Main clustering loop\n    while (!unclustered_indices.empty()) {\n        int max_cardinality = -1;\n        int best_seed = -1;\n        std::vector<int> best_cluster_members;\n        \n        // Try each unclustered point as a seed\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < unclustered_indices.size(); ++i) {\n            const int seed = unclustered_indices[i];\n            if (clustered[seed]) continue;\n            \n            std::vector<int> candidate_members;\n            const int cardinality = generateCandidateCluster(seed, clustered, points, \n                                                       threshold, N, \n                                                       &candidate_members);\n            \n            if (cardinality > max_cardinality) {\n                max_cardinality = cardinality;\n                best_seed = seed;\n                best_cluster_members = candidate_members;\n            }\n        }\n        \n        // If we found a cluster, add it\n        if (best_seed >= 0 && max_cardinality > 0) {\n            Cluster cluster;\n            cluster.seed_point = best_seed;\n            cluster.members = best_cluster_members;\n            clusters.push_back(cluster);\n            \n            // Mark all members as clustered\n            for (size_t i = 0; i < best_cluster_members.size(); ++i) {\n                clustered[best_cluster_members[i]] = true;\n            }\n            \n            // Remove clustered points from unclustered list\n            unclustered_indices.erase(\n                std::remove_if(unclustered_indices.begin(), unclustered_indices.end(),\n                              [&clustered](int idx) { return clustered[idx]; }),\n                unclustered_indices.end()\n            );\n        } else {\n            // No more clusters can be formed\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return clusters;\n}\n\n// Validation: check that clusters satisfy the QT clustering properties\nbool validateClusters(const std::vector<Cluster>& clusters,\n                     const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                     const double threshold) {\n    bool valid = true;\n    \n    printf(\"Validating clusters:\\n\");\n    \n    // Check each cluster\n    for (size_t c = 0; c < clusters.size(); ++c) {\n        const auto& cluster = clusters[c];\n        double max_diameter = 0.0;\n        \n        // Check diameter (max distance between any two points)\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < cluster.members.size(); ++i) {\n            for (size_t j = i + 1; j < cluster.members.size(); ++j) {\n                const double dist = distance(points[cluster.members[i]], \n                                           points[cluster.members[j]]);\n                max_diameter = std::max(max_diameter, dist);\n            }\n        }\n        \n        if (c < 10) { // Print first 10 clusters\n            printf(\"  Cluster %zu: size=%zu, seed=%d, diameter=%.4f\\n\", \n                   c, cluster.members.size(), cluster.seed_point, max_diameter);\n        }\n        \n        // Validate diameter is within threshold\n        if (max_diameter valid = false;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Check for duplicate memberships\n    std::vector<int> membership(points.size(), -1);\n    for (size_t c = 0; c < clusters.size(); ++c) {\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < clusters[c].members.size(); ++i) {\n            const int member = clusters[c].members[i];\n            if (membership[member] >= 0) {\n                printf(\"ERROR: Point %d appears in multiple clusters (%d and %zu)\\n\",\n                       member, membership[member], c);\n                valid = false;\n            }\n            membership[member] = static_cast<int>(c);\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Count clustered points\n    int clustered_count = 0;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < membership.size(); ++i) {\n        if (membership[i] >= 0) clustered_count++;\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Total points: %zu, Clustered: %d, Unclustered: %zu\\n\",\n           points.size(), clustered_count, points.size() - clustered_count);\n    \n    return     num_points = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-t\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            threshold = atof(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n Clustering Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Number of points: %d\\n\", num_points);\n    printf(\"Distance threshold: %.2f\\n\", threshold);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1792957033141,"sessionID":"ses_e8b6fde83ffee9kpLlM4ivS7oD","part":{"id":"prt_174903b94001tJQ1d86ubp7VTr","messageID":"msg_17490381c001Xi1uw6N301Xc5X","sessionID":"ses_e8b6fde83ffee9kpLlM4ivS7oD","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm working through the QT clustering algorithm's semantics: iterating over unclustered points in order, generating candidate clusters for each seed, and selecting the one with the largest cardinality, breaking ties by picking the first one found.\n\nIn generateCandidateCluster, I note the growth logic adds the closest unclustered point to the current members—where \"closest\" means minimizing the maximum distance to any existing cluster member, as long as that maximum distance stays under both the threshold and the smallest diameter seen so far, with ties resolved by lowest index.\n\nThe algorithm as written is extremely expensive—roughly O(N) seeds times O(N) growth steps times O(N) candidate scans times O(members) distance calculations, which balloons toward O(N^4) for N=1000. For GPU parallelization, the key optimization is maintaining a running max-distance array per candidate and updating it incrementally each time a new member is added, rather than recomputing the max from scratch—this preserves exact floating-point equivalence while avoiding redundant work.\n\nI need to be careful about floating-point contraction though: distance squared is symmetric since negation is exact in IEEE arithmetic, but FMA contraction (common on both GPU via nvcc and CPU via GCC's default fp-contract=fast under gnu++20) could change bit-level results between implementations, so I may need explicit non-contracting intrinsics to guarantee bitwise equivalence.\n\nRather than guessing whether the CPU build uses FMA, my safest approach is to build the original as a reference binary outside the workspace and empirically compare outputs across many parameter sets. I should also keep validation logic on the CPU, and avoid comparing squared distances instead of sqrt values since the monotonic transformation could shift results right at threshold boundaries.\n\nFor parallelization, I'm thinking each unclustered seed's candidate cluster growth is independent, so I can assign one thread block per seed and reduce across seeds afterward to select the best by cardinality with lowest-index tie-breaking. Within each seed's growth, the steps are sequential, but each step's candidate search can be parallelized across threads in the block with a reduction to find the argmin by maxdist and index tie-break.\n\nAfter computing per-thread values, I'd do a block-level reduction to find the argmin, breaking ties by lowest index, then sync and add the winner — repeating for however many steps the cluster needs, with N blocks giving good parallelism. I'm also checking that the incremental max-distance update stays mathematically equivalent to recomputing the max over all members each time.\n\nSince clustered status stays fixed during a seed's growth and candidates exclude members already in the cluster, termination works the same way as the original: loop until no eligible candidate remains, matching findClosest returning -1. Finally, best-cluster selection just needs to pick the seed with the largest cluster, breaking ties by the smallest seed index.\n\nFor reconstructing membership, I realize storing full member lists for every seed is too memory-heavy at scale (O(N²)), so instead I should only track cardinalities in a first pass, then re-run the deterministic growth process just for the winning seed to recover its actual member list.\n\nThis two-phase approach adds one extra growth computation per cluster but keeps memory light, and the kernel launch overhead across many cluster iterations should still be manageable for reasonable N.\n\nI'm weighing whether to make growth block-cooperative: one block per seed with 256 threads handling candidates works, but storing per-block distance arrays scales poorly—8MB is fine for N=1000, but for 100k seeds the memory balloons to tens of gigabytes, so I need to chunk the launches instead of processing everything at once.\n\nI'm deciding to batch seeds within a memory budget, since recomputing distances from scratch each step is too costly and incremental tracking per seed is necessary. I'm also checking whether shared memory could substitute for global scratch—it works for small N but not generally, so global memory with a per-seed availability flag array seems like the right compromise.\n\nFor the growth routine, I'm planning to keep separate scratch arrays for max distance and cluster membership rather than merging them with sentinels, favoring clarity. The best-candidate selection at each step needs to find the minimum eligible distance that's also below both the threshold and current best diameter, breaking ties by lowest index.\n\nFor the incremental update, after adding a member I only need to update maxdist for candidates not yet in the cluster by taking the max against the new member's distance, starting from the seed's own contribution in the first step. I'm sketching out the initialization logic now.\n\nSince maxd only increases monotonically, once a candidate falls below threshold ineligibility, it stays ineligible permanently—so pruning isn't strictly necessary. I also note the seed itself gets marked in-cluster and skipped from future candidacy, consistent with how clustered status is tracked during cluster growth.\n\nFor the argmin reduction, I'm designing each thread to track its local best value/index using strict comparison with index tie-breaking, then combining across threads via warp shuffle and shared memory reduction. I'm considering packing value and index into a single 64-bit key, since non-negative doubles preserve ordering when reinterpreted as unsigned integers, which would simplify the comparison logic.\n\nFor the kernel structure, I'm planning blockDim of 256 threads per block, with each block handling one seed's growth and writing out its final cardinality. After all batches complete, the host picks the seed with maximum cardinality, breaking ties by lowest index since seeds are processed in ascending order.\n\nThe phase 1 kernel only computes cardinalities cheaply, while a separate phase 2 kernel reruns growth on just the winning seed to record its actual member list — this avoids storing all U×N member arrays and the extra growth cost is negligible relative to scanning all U seeds. On the host side, I'll keep the clustered/unclustered tracking similar to the original, maintaining an ascending vector of unclustered points and uploading seed batches as needed.\n\nFor small N (hundreds to low thousands), per-iteration host/device syncs and full clustered-array re-uploads are trivial in cost, since the real bottleneck is the phase 1 seed evaluation work, not the bookkeeping. I'll store points as a simple two-double struct that's trivially copyable to the device, and the distance computation itself is a straightforward Euclidean calculation between point coordinates.\n\nNow I'm worried about floating-point consistency between CPU and GPU: compiler FMA contraction could fuse the multiply-add in the distance formula differently depending on platform (nvcc vs GCC with -march=native), causing subtle mismatches versus the original unfused computation. To get deterministic IEEE behavior on the device I could use explicit non-fused add/multiply intrinsics, but I need to actually verify via compiled assembly whether the original CPU code gets contracted at all before deciding whether to force `-ffp-contract=off` anywhere.\n\nFor the build setup, since I can't create new files, I'll keep qtclustering.cpp as-is but mark it as CUDA via CMake's `set_source_files_properties` with LANGUAGE CUDA, enabling CUDA as a project language so nvcc compiles it while keeping the same filename. I also need to set the CUDA architecture target appropriately for an RTX 3090 (sm_86), using `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native` if the CMake version supports it, otherwise specifying it explicitly.\n\nAdding compiler flag options...\n\nSkipping -lineinfo. I also need to make sure the device code includes the CUDA runtime header and a CUDA_CHECK macro, and note that CMake's CUDA language support automatically links cudart.\n\nI'm keeping the `m` library link and leaving -march=native and rand_r-based host data generation untouched, since clustering timing already wraps the whole GPU function including transfers. I'll remove the unused CPU-only helper functions like findClosestPoint and generateCandidateCluster and replace qtClustering with the GPU version to keep the code clean.\n\nI'm double-checking edge cases: N=1 works fine through both growth phases, the threshold comparison matches the device version exactly, and the original cardinality tie-breaking (favoring the lowest index) is preserved in my argmax logic. Now I'm working out batched scratch memory allocation per seed, sizing buffers for distances and membership flags based on an available budget.\n\nNext I'm drafting the device distance function using fused multiply-add intrinsics, then sketching the block-cooperative cluster growth routine with shared memory buffers for warp-level reductions of distance values and indices.\n\nStill writing clustering logic...\n\nThread 0 marks the chosen index as included, adds it to membership, increments the count, and updates cur, with a sync afterward. I need to make sure there's a syncthreads right after that update so other threads reading inC in the next iteration see the consistent state.\n\nI'm now designing a block-wide argmin reduction helper that first does a warp-level shuffle reduction to find the minimum value and its index, then combines results across warps using shared memory, ensuring proper syncs between the write and broadcast-read of the shared best value. Writing warp reduction logic...\n\nI'm realizing there's a genuine race here: the shared slot s_v[0] gets overwritten by warp 0 lane 0 in the next reduction's first phase, before any __syncthreads guards it, so a thread that's lagging on reading the previous result could collide with that write.\n\nSince cur is only set by thread 0 before the sync, pts[cur] stays read-only and safe. The break condition relies on bi from the broadcast being identical across threads, so that stays uniform too, and the member recording just has thread 0 write bi into outMembers[count]. Now I'm moving on to the phase 1 kernel.\n\nEach block processes one seed from the batch, using its own slice of the scratch arrays for max-distance and in-cluster tracking, with thread 0 writing the resulting cluster size to the output array. For phase 2, I'm using a single block to grow the final cluster, writing both the member list and the count, allowing the members pointer to be null during phase 1 since it's not needed there. On the host side, I'm sketching out the overall GPU clustering flow — allocating and copying the points, tracking clustered status, maintaining the list of unclustered indices, and sizing the batch scratch buffers for seeds, max-distances, and inclusion flags.\n\nI'm working out the main loop: while unclustered points remain, batch through seeds, launch the kernel per batch, copy back cluster sizes, and track the best seed/cluster found so far. If no valid cluster is found, I break out, otherwise I rerun growth on the best seed to extract the actual member list and finalize that cluster before removing its members from the unclustered set.\n\nI'm double-checking a few details for consistency with the original algorithm — the clustered-flag check in phase 1 is a no-op, the seed and member removal logic should stay in lock-step with the host-side unclustered vector, and I'm sizing the scratch buffers based on a memory budget to decide the max batch size per iteration.\n\nNow I want to set up a baseline: copy the original reference implementation into a temp directory preserving its relative includes, build it, and run it with several parameters to capture reference outputs before making changes. Since the reference is likely quite slow for larger N, I should time this carefully, and it's worth tracking the overall task with a short todo list before proceeding.\n\n","time":{"start":1792956971924,"end":1792957032977},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

maximum distance to the cluster incrementally, and a block-wide argmin\n//     (ties broken by lowest index) selects the winner.\n//   - The host selects the seed with the largest cluster (ties broken by the\n//     lowest point index, as in the sequential scan), then re-grows that seed\n//     once to record its members in insertion order.\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <cfloat>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <climits>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdint>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nstatic const double MAX_WIDTH = 20.0;\nstatic const double MAX_HEIGHT = 20.0;\n\n// Threads per block used for per-seed cluster growth\nstatic const int BLOCK_THREADS = 256;\nstatic const int WARP_SIZE = 32;\n\n// Upper bound on device scratch memory used for per-seed working state\nstatic const size_t SCRATCH_BUDGET_BYTES = size_t(1) << 30;\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                        \\\n    do {                                                                        \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                              \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                              \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,    \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                  \\\n            exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                 \\\n        }                                                                       \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Structure to represent a point in 2D space\nstruct Point {\n    double x, y;\n};\n\n// Structure to represent a cluster\nstruct Cluster {\n    std::vector<int> members;\n    int seed_point;\n};\n\n// Generate synthetic 2D point data in clusters\nvoid generateSyntheticData(std::vector<Point>& points, const int N, unsigned int seed = 42) {\n    auto frand = [&seed]() mutable { return rand_r(&seed) / static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX); };\n    \n    const double min_dim = std::min(MAX_WIDTH, MAX_HEIGHT);\n    int count = 0;\n    \n    while (count < N) {\n        // Create group_cnt points within a circle of radius R\n        // around center point (cntr_x, cntr_y)\n        const double cntr_x = frand() * MAX_WIDTH;\n        const double cntr_y = frand() * MAX_HEIGHT;\n        const double R = frand() * min_dim / 2.0;\n        int group_cnt = static_cast<int>(frand() * (N / 30.0));\n        \n        // Make sure we don't make more points than we need\n        if (group_cnt > (N - count)) {\n            group_cnt = N - count;\n        }\n        \n        while (group_cnt > 0) {\n            const double sign = (frand() < 0.5) ? -1.0 : 1.0;\n            const double r = frand() * R;\n            const double dx = (2.0 * frand() - 1.0) * r;\n            const double dy = std::sqrt(r * r - dx * dx) * sign;\n            const double x = cntr_x + dx;\n            const double y = cntr_y + dy;\n            \n            if (x < 0 || x > MAX_WIDTH || y < 0 || y > MAX_HEIGHT) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            \n            points[count] = {x, y};\n            count++;\n            group_cnt--;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Calculate Euclidean distance between two points (host, used for validation)\ninline double distance(const Point& p1, const Point& p2) {\n    double dx = p1.x - p2.x;\n    double dy = p1.y - p2.y;\n    return std::sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);\n}\n\n// Device-side distance. Uses the same operation order and fused multiply-add\n// as the host build, so the distances (and therefore all comparisons) match.\n__device__ __forceinline__ double distanceDevice(const Point& p1, const Point& p2) {\n    const double dx = p1.x - p2.x;\n    const double dy = p1.y - p2.y;\n    return __dsqrt_rn(__fma_rn(dx, dx, __dmul_rn(dy, dy)));\n}\n\n// Ordering used for argmin: smaller value wins, ties go to the lower index\n__device__ __forceinline__ bool argminBetter(double v1, int i1, double v2, int i2) {\n    return v1 < v2 || (v1 == v2 && i1 < i2);\n}\n\n// Warp-level argmin; the result is valid in lane 0\n__device__ __forceinline__ void warpArgmin(double& v, int& i) {\n    for (int offset = WARP_SIZE / 2; offset > 0; offset >>= 1) {\n        const double ov = __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffffu, v, offset);\n        const int oi = __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffffu, i, offset);\n        if (argminBetter(ov, oi, v, i)) {\n            v = ov;\n            i = oi;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Block-wide argmin. On return every thread holds the same (v, i) pair.\n// sv and si must provide at least WARP_SIZE entries each.\n__device__ __forceinline__ void blockArgmin(double& v, int& i, double* sv, int* si) {\n    warpArgmin(v, i);\n\n    const int lane = threadIdx.x & (WARP_SIZE - 1);\n    const int warp = threadIdx.x / WARP_SIZE;\n    if (lane == 0) {\n        sv[warp] = v;\n        si[warp] = i;\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    if (warp == 0) {\n        const int numWarps = blockDim.x / WARP_SIZE;\n        v = (lane < numWarps) ? sv[lane] : INFINITY;\n        i = (lane < numWarps) ? si[lane] : INT_MAX;\n        warpArgmin(v, i);\n        if (lane == 0) {\n            sv[0] = v;\n            si[0] = i;\n        }\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    v = sv[0];\n    i = si[0];\n}\n\n// Grow the candidate cluster starting from `seed` (block-cooperative).\n// Must be called by all threads of the block with identical arguments except\n// that `members` may be nullptr. Returns the cluster cardinality.\n//   maxd[c]   : running max distance from candidate c to current members\n//   inCluster : membership flags for points in the growing cluster\n__device__ int growCandidateCluster(const int seed,\n                                    const Point* points,\n                                    const uint8_t* clustered,\n                                    double* maxd,\n                                    uint8_t* inCluster,\n                                    const int N,\n                                    const double threshold,\n                                    int* members,\n                                    double* sv,\n                                    int* si) {\n    for (int c = threadIdx.x; c < N; c += blockDim.x) {\n        maxd[c] = 0.0;\n        inCluster[c] = 0;\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    if (threadIdx.x == 0) {\n        inCluster[seed] = 1;\n        if (members) members[0] = seed;\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    int count = 1;\n    int current = seed;\n\n    while (count < N) {\n        double bestVal = INFINITY;\n        int bestIdx = INT_MAX;\n\n        for (int c = threadIdx.x; c < N; c += blockDim.x) {\n            if (clustered[c] || inCluster[c]) continue;\n\n            // Running max over members == max over all members of the cluster\n            const double d = distanceDevice(points[c], points[current]);\n            const double m = std::max(maxd[c], d);\n            maxd[c] = m;\n\n            if (m < threshold && m < bestVal) {\n                bestVal = m;\n                bestIdx = c;\n            }\n        }\n\n        blockArgmin(bestVal, bestIdx, sv, si);\n\n        // Uniform across the block: all threads hold the same bestIdx\n        if (bestIdx == INT_MAX) break;\n\n        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {\n            inCluster[bestIdx] = 1;\n            if (members) members[count] = bestIdx;\n        }\n        current = bestIdx;\n        count++;\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    return count;\n}\n\n// One block per seed: computes the cardinality of the candidate cluster\n__global__ void seedCardinalityKernel(const int* seeds,\n cardinalities) {\n    __shared__ double sv[WARP_SIZE];\n    __shared__ int si[WARP_SIZE];\n\n    const int b = blockIdx.x;\n    const size_t base = static_cast<size_t>(b) * static_cast<size_t>(N);\n    const int card = growCandidateCluster(seeds[b], points, clustered,\n                                          maxdAll + base, inClusterAll + base,\n                                          N, threshold, nullptr, sv, si);\n    if (threadIdx.x == 0) {\n        cardinalities[b] = card;\n    }\n}\n\n// Single block: re-grows the chosen seed and records its members in order\n__global__ void runtime (context creation) outside of timed sections\nvoid initCuda() {\n    int deviceCount = 0;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceCount(&deviceCount));\n    if (deviceCount == 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"Error: no CUDA-capable device found\\n\");\n        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(nullptr));\n}\n\n// Main QT clustering algorithm (GPU)\nstd::vector<Cluster>  CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_points, sizeof(Point) * N));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_clustered, sizeof(uint8_t) * N));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_seeds, sizeof(int) * N));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_cards, sizeof(int) * batchMax));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_maxd, sizeof(double) * batchMax * N));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_inCluster, sizeof(uint8_t) * batchMax * N));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_members, sizeof(int) * N));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_count, sizeof(int)));\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(d_points, points.data(), sizeof(Point) * N,  std::vector<int> hCards(batchMax);\n\n    // Main clustering loop\n    while (!unclustered_indices.empty()) {\n        const int U = static_cast<int>(unclustered_indices.size());\n        int max_cardinality = -1;\n        int best_seed = -1;\n\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(d_seeds, unclustered_indices.data(), sizeof(int) * U,\n                              cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n seed (in batches)\n        for (int start = 0; start < U; start += static_cast<int>(batchMax)) {\n            const int n = std::min(static_cast<int>(batchMax), U - start);\n\n if (best_seed >= 0 && max_cardinality > 0) {\n            recordClusterKernel<<<1, BLOCK_THREADS>>>(best_seed, d_points, d_clustered, N,\n
